title: Odds too high where the engine had a story
evidence: Program 2's four bets were given 55-70%; none came back a clear hit (two fails, one undetermined, one untestable). Over all nine scored bets the engine's Brier score (0.236) is worse than always saying the running base rate (0.173), and the two hits were given 25%, below several misses: the odds do not yet rank bets.
do_this: Start from the running base rate ((passes + 1) / (resolved + 2), 3/11 = 0.27 at 16:46) and move away from it only for a named reason. Odds above 0.5 need evidence from a pilot or an archive, not a plausible mechanism.
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: A null-type rule with no power check or equivalence margin, reported as a pass
evidence: om-p2-4's rule was 'the CI of the error difference includes 0'. The minimum detectable effect was about 0.084 against a comparison error of 0.097, so the test could not have seen the difference. Audit round 2 reversed it to undetermined. Round 1 found the same in v2-run-1 (no equivalence margin; MDE about 0.10).
do_this: Any 'no difference' or 'no better than' pass rule pre-registers an equivalence margin and a power check (MDE below the margin) from a pilot or the archive. Without one, it is not a bet.
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: No dumb baseline: a trivial predictor would pass the rule
evidence: om-p2-2's pooled Q 0.50 is almost all condition label (label-only predictor 0.477). Opus's F' 'one belief' pass is matched by a one-bit 'rating above 50' predictor (Q 0.88). In round 1, a one-bit 'model said no' predictor tied the v1 error-prediction arms (AUROC 0.675), and item type alone scored 0.71 on v2.
do_this: Pre-register the dumbest predictor that could pass (constant, one-bit, label-only, noiseless) and make the rule 'beat it by a margin', not 'clear a fixed bar'.
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: A manipulation that never took effect: the code did not do what the pre-registration says
evidence: ng-p3-1 never loaded the job-time T1/T2 (qiskit returns a copy of qubit_properties, so the assignment was discarded), and its E2 ZZ term was never applied (local CZ errors override the all-qubit default); counts were identical at ZZ 0, 0.1 and 1.0 rad. The run used a different model from the one described. The verdict survived by luck.
do_this: Before the first call, dry-run every manipulation at two settings and check the output moves, and print the parameters the run will actually use (operators/design-review.md, check D2).
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: Unmatched rivals: the contest is decided by how the families were built
evidence: ng-p3-5's coherent family is unitary on the reference state, so it cannot change purity; the chip's states had lost purity, so on h221 no coherent model could win. A joint fit finds coherent terms on every pair, contradicting 'blur, not steering'.
do_this: Check that each rival can, in principle, reproduce the other's best case on synthetic data before the real fit (design-review check D4).
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: A control that cannot fail
evidence: ng-p3-1's control band [0.221, 0.281] is also passed by a noiseless simulator (0.279), so it cannot tell a faithful noisy rebuild from no noise at all.
do_this: For every control, name a wrong set-up it must reject and show that it does (design-review check D3).
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: A foreseeable execution risk run without a pilot
evidence: om-p2-3 stopped on an API refusal after 26 calls, on a severity-3 explosives story; 552 of the 1,147 SimpleToM stories are severity 3. Its pre-mortem named the risk, and the design accepted it without a pilot.
do_this: When the pre-mortem names an execution risk, pilot it first on items excluded from the test (at most $0.10), or filter the items by a rule written before the pilot.
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: Comparing across conditions that differ in more than the factor named
evidence: '0.502 on 3 November against 0.246 today' compares a circuit with a pre-measurement barrier, run as one 1,000-shot block, with one without it, run as interleaved 100-shot pieces. In round 1, own-versus-other differed in instruction, schema and turn position, not only in whose number it was.
do_this: List every difference between the two conditions being compared. If more than the named factor differs, the claim is about the bundle, or the design matches them.
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: The right rule, then the wrong noun
evidence: Frozen rules applied correctly, then reported with words the design cannot carry: 'credence' (Opus F'), 'not steering' (ng-p3-5), 'names the self' (om-p2-1), 'knows itself about as well' (om-p2-4), 'one unusual afternoon' (ng-p3-2/3). Round 2's commonest fault; round 1's was numbers stated more strongly than the data.
do_this: Write the plain-English sentence for each possible verdict in the pre-registration (§5), before data, and use only those sentences afterwards.
written_by: engine session (Claude), from the ledger and audit rounds 1-2, 2026-11-04 16:46 America/Denver

title: A label that hangs on one item
evidence: h058 decides 3 of 5 multi-model labels, h191 decides the probe study's 'not with the rating' on both draws, and in round 1 two of ten items drove most of direction 2.
do_this: Pre-register leave-one-item-out as a reported robustness check, and state in the verdict rule what happens if one item flips the label.
